metaDescription: Switches that move a chosen load to generator power, from 15A circuit boxes to 60A and 100A double-pole units and a 200A whole-panel switch.
expertTake: The Generac 60 Amp manual switch is the pick for anyone building an essential-loads subpanel, because it is double-pole, sized for a subpanel and a single clear job. The Nature's Generator 15A 4-circuit box is the value pick when the load list is short. A household that wants every breaker live on generator power should price the 200A Tzechkii and a bigger generator together.
introParagraphs: Every transfer switch is really a way of choosing a load. You decide what the generator will carry and the switch makes sure that load, and only that load, leaves the utility. Whether the load is one appliance, a subpanel of essentials or the whole house changes everything about the purchase.

That framing makes the choice clearer than starting with brand or amps. List the loads that matter, add the startup surge of the motors, and compare the total with what your generator can deliver. Then pick a switch whose scope matches that list instead of one that is simply the biggest you can afford.

products.name: Generac 60A manual double-pole switch for a dedicated load
products.description:
A subpanel of essential circuits is the natural partner for this switch. The listing describes single-load transfer to a dedicated load, 60 amp capacity that supports subpanels or essential household appliances, and double-pole switching that manually isolates the generator from utility service to prevent backfeed. In plain terms, you move one feeder, not twelve separate circuits.

That design keeps the generator's burden in check: whatever you place on the subpanel is all the generator will ever see. It is simpler to wire than a multi-circuit kit, because the electrician builds the subpanel once and the switch has just two sources and one output. Against the Nature's 15A 4-circuit box, it handles far more current, and against the 100A Generac it saves cost and size for a smaller generator.

The ownership chore is discipline about what lives in the subpanel. Keep a typed schedule of its breakers, add loads only deliberately and run the generator monthly. Exercise the lever twice a year with everything off, and note the position of the handle in the manual so a house sitter can follow it. A laminated card on the subpanel door that reads utility, off, generator in the order the handle moves removes most of the guesswork on a stressful night.
products.bestFor: A moderate essential-loads subpanel fed by a mid-size portable generator.
pros: 60A suits a subpanel or large appliance feed
Double-pole switching isolates from the utility
One feeder keeps generator load predictable
Manual design with no electronics
cons: Needs a subpanel built by an electrician
One load path only, no per-circuit rockers

products.name: Generac 100A manual double-pole generator transfer switch
products.description:
High capacity is the selling point here: the listing says the 100 amp rating supports high-demand loads during extended outages, using double-pole manual switching that isolates the generator from utility service. It is the larger sibling of the 60A switch with the same single-load concept.

The extra 40 amps matter when the feeder will serve a whole subpanel with a well pump, a water heater and a furnace. Compared with the 60A, it costs more and suits bigger generators, and compared with the 200A Tzechkii it still limits you to one chosen load rather than the entire service. That boundary is what keeps a portable generator from being overwhelmed.

As always with larger amperage, plan an electrician and permit, and ask for a one-line diagram. Keep the feeder breaker labeled and review the subpanel list each year. A 100A rating does not mean 100A of generator, so check the generator's real output before assuming the switch's capacity is usable. Many buyers discover only after the install that a 7,500 watt generator can feed less than a third of what the switch can pass, which is fine, as long as the subpanel was planned around the engine and not the switch.
products.bestFor: A larger subpanel with a well pump and water heater on a big generator.
pros: 100A capacity for high-demand subpanels
Double-pole manual isolation
Single-load design limits generator burden
Same layout as the 60A, scaled up
cons: Higher tier than the 60A for capacity many cannot use
Needs a licensed electrician and permit

products.name: Nature's Generator 15A 4-circuit 120V transfer switch
products.description:
Selecting by circuit rather than by feeder is the alternative approach, and this is the smallest example. Four circuits at 15 amps and 120 volts add up to roughly 1,800 watts, and each circuit has its own manual selector so you can drop one at a time when fuel or output runs short. UL listing is named in the title.

That per-circuit control is the point of a load switch. With the Generac 60A feeding a subpanel, every breaker on the subpanel rides along. Here you move only what you flip, which makes it ideal for a short list: refrigerator, a few lights, a modem and a furnace blower. It cannot reach a 240V load.

Care is easy but must be regular. Exercise the selectors twice a year, keep a written list of which circuit is which and mark the one that serves the furnace in red. When fuel gets low late in an outage, dropping the freezer for an hour is easier than shutting down the whole generator, and four independent selectors make that possible. When the list grows beyond four loads, treat that as the sign to move to a subpanel or a larger kit rather than overloading the box.
products.bestFor: A short list of 120V loads on a small generator.
pros: Four selectable circuits for fine load control
UL listing cited in the title
Easy to explain and operate
Lowest capacity and footprint of the manual kits
cons: About 1,800W ceiling is easy to outgrow

products.name: Tzechkii 200A manual double-throw switch, NEMA 3R
products.description:
Moving everything at once is the opposite of a load switch, and that makes this a useful extreme. It is a double-throw disconnect with a manual lever in a galvanized NEMA 3R enclosure, rated 200A at 120/240V, which shifts the whole service between the utility and a generator. The 48,000 watt label is a theoretical ceiling.

In practice, putting the whole panel on a generator moves the load decision from the hardware to the household. Every breaker becomes live, so a clothes dryer, a range and the central air are all one careless switch-on away from stalling a portable generator. It suits owners with a large generator and the discipline to turn big loads off, and it is a poor match for a household where several people share the decisions.

An electrician installs it at the service entrance. Ask for a written start-up order, post it inside the panel door and walk the house turning off the largest loads before the lever moves. Inspect the enclosure each spring for rust at the screw heads and cut edges. Because the lever moves the entire service, also confirm that the cover interlock still prevents the door from opening while the lever is in motion, and report any play to the installer.
products.bestFor: Large generators and households that will manage loads by habit.
pros: 200A rating covers the full service
Galvanized NEMA 3R enclosure
Manual lever with no electronics
All breakers remain usable
cons: Service-level work requires a licensed electrician

products.name: YAURILO 15A automatic transfer relay, NEMA 5-15P/R

specList.label: Sources
specList.value: Utility or shore plus inverter or generator

products.description:
One appliance, one plug and no lever: that is the scope of this automatic relay. It switches between a utility or shore power input and an inverter or generator input, with a NEMA 5-15 plug and receptacle, and describes a waterproof, moisture-proof plastic shell for indoor or outdoor use.

It is the smallest load switch in the group, ideal for a freezer, an aquarium or a sump pump that is already plugged into an outlet. It does not isolate with a mechanical break the way the Generac double-pole switches do, and it needs a generator that is already running to take over. For that reason it complements rather than replaces a proper panel switch.

To use it well, plug the appliance into the receptacle side, the utility cord into one input and the generator cord into the other, then label all three. Check the plug ends for heat marks every season. Do not extend the load beyond 15A, and keep the relay off the floor where water can reach it. A freezer in a damp basement is where this device most often lives, so mount it a hand's width above the highest water mark you have seen.
products.bestFor: A single plug-in appliance such as a freezer or sump pump.
pros: Automatic switchover with no lever
Plug-in design needs no panel work
Waterproof shell claimed for indoor or outdoor
Works with inverter or generator input
cons: Needs the generator running before it can take over

buyingCriteria.explanation: A single appliance calls for the YAURILO relay, a short list calls for the Nature's 15A 4-circuit box, a subpanel calls for the Generac 60A or 100A and the whole house calls for the Tzechkii 200A. Starting with scope prevents buying a switch whose size or type does not match the plan. Write the list before you open a catalog, and walk the house with the panel open, writing the breaker number beside each item so you know exactly which wires the switch will touch.

The Generac switches move one feeder, so everything on the subpanel goes together. The Nature's box lets you drop a circuit at a time. If fuel or output runs short, selectors give finer control, while a feeder is simpler to wire.

Both Generac listings state double-pole switching that isolates the generator from utility service. That is the mechanism that prevents backfeed on a 240V feed. Avoid any manual scheme that does not clearly break both hot legs.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Amp rating against real generator output
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 100A switch does not make a 5,000 watt generator deliver 24,000 watts. The practical limit is the engine. Pick the switch that fits the subpanel's real load, not the biggest number. If the subpanel will only ever carry 30A of loads, a 100A switch is a safe but unnecessary expense, and the money is better spent on a quieter or larger generator.

A well pump or air conditioner draws several times its running current for a moment. The subpanel's total load must leave room for the biggest surge. Start motors one at a time, largest first, because a generator that is already carrying a steady load has less reserve to catch a surge than one starting from idle.

The YAURILO plugs in, the Nature's box is wired into the panel and the Generac and Tzechkii switches tie into feeders or the service. The higher the rating, the more clearly an electrician is required. Check local permit rules before buying, and ask whether the inspector wants a diagram of the subpanel. Many jurisdictions treat a transfer switch and its subpanel as one inspected assembly, so submit them together.

specDecoder.meaning: A switch that opens both hot conductors of a 240V feed. It is needed to fully isolate a split-phase circuit.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Generac 60A and 100A both list double-pole switching.

specDecoder.meaning: The switch moves one feeder or dedicated load between sources, not many circuits independently.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Generac listings use this phrase; the Nature's box offers per-circuit selectors instead.

specDecoder.meaning: A lever that connects the load to one of two sources and never both.
A secondary breaker box that holds the circuits you want on the generator. It is fed through the transfer switch.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 60A or 100A switch assumes a subpanel built by an electrician.

specDecoder.meaning: A device that moves between sources by itself when it senses power. It needs a running generator.
specDecoder.watchFor: The YAURILO is automatic and limited to 15A.

howWeEvaluated.title: Match to load scope
howWeEvaluated.description: We sorted the picks by how much they move: one appliance, four circuits, a subpanel or the whole panel. Each scope suits a different household. A mismatched scope is the usual regret.

howWeEvaluated.title: Isolation mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for double-pole switching, double-throw levers or interlocks. The Generac and Tzechkii listings describe this plainly. A listing silent on isolation lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity ladder
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the 15A, 60A, 100A and 200A steps against typical generator output. The ladder shows where capacity exceeds what a portable can supply. This is based on spec sheets, not lab work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control granularity
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted whether the switch lets you shed loads one at a time. The Nature's selectors win here. Granularity matters when fuel runs low.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation level
howWeEvaluated.description: We rated how much professional work each pick needs, from a plug-in relay to a service-entrance switch. Cost of labor belongs in any comparison.

cards.label: Subpanel feed
cards.text: The Generac 60A and 100A feed a subpanel, so the electrician moves your essential circuits there once. Operation is a single handle. The cost is the subpanel build, which also forces a useful clean-up of what the household truly counts as essential.

cards.label: Circuit selectors
cards.text: The Nature's 15A box wires each chosen circuit to its own selector. You can drop a load without touching the others. It suits short lists and small generators.

howToChoose.note: Choose a subpanel for a long list and selectors when you want to ration load by hand.

howToChoose.subheading: For Well Pump and Water Heater Loads Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 240V pump and an electric water heater need double-pole switching and a feeder rated for their combined current. Add the pump's startup surge and keep the heater off until the pump is running.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Generac 60A suits a subpanel with a pump and lights, the 100A covers a pump plus a water heater, and the Tzechkii leaves everything live. The Nature's 15A box cannot feed 240V loads.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your essentials include several 240V loads or you plan a larger generator, which points to the Generac 100A. Pay for a clean subpanel layout, not for extra amps alone.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if the list is short. The Nature's 15A box and the YAURILO relay cost the least and cover small jobs.

maintenance.why: Contacts that never move build oxidation. Cycle them with the generator off.
New appliances creep onto the essential subpanel. A written schedule keeps the generator load honest.
Transfer the real load and start motors one at a time. It reveals surge problems before a storm.
Heat marks and rust signal trouble. Have an electrician retorque if needed.
Heat-marked plugs and cracked jackets are fire risks. Replace them.

faq.q: What is a load transfer switch?
faq.a: It moves a chosen load from the utility to a generator and back, isolating the two so power never flows into the grid. The load can be one appliance, a few circuits, a subpanel or the whole house.

faq.q: Is a 100A switch better than a 60A?
faq.a: Only if your subpanel's load needs it. Both are double-pole and manual. The 100A suits bigger subpanels, while the 60A fits most essential-loads setups on a mid-size generator.

faq.q: Why not just use the 200A whole-panel switch?
faq.a: It leaves every breaker live, so a portable generator is easy to overload. It suits large generators and disciplined households. A subpanel keeps the load limited by design.

faq.q: Can I install a subpanel myself?
faq.a: In most places no. It involves moving circuits and a permit, and a licensed electrician is normally required. Ask your building department.

faq.q: Do automatic relays replace a transfer switch?
faq.a: Only for a single plug-in appliance. The YAURILO handles one 15A device. Hardwired circuits need a proper manual or automatic transfer switch.

faq.q: How do I avoid overloading the generator?
faq.a: List your loads, add the largest motor's startup surge and start big loads one at a time. A subpanel with a written schedule keeps the total predictable.
